column1: #  Target T1: peroxygenase conversion fraction on 4-propylguaiacol, per enzyme, at three pH values.
#  Source: Figure S8 of Barros-Reguera et al. 2025, DOI 10.1186/s13068-025-02675-w (PMC12306115).
#  These are PRINTED DATA LABELS on the figure, not bar heights measured by eye. Where a stacked bar
#  carries no green label the peroxygenase fraction is recorded as 0; the figure prints a label for every
#  non-zero green segment, so 0 means "no labelled peroxygenase product", not "missing".
#  Caption, verbatim (abridged): "Fractions of peroxygenase conversion and non-converted substrate in
#  reactions with ascorbic acid for 19 different UPOs at three different pH values... The peroxygenase
#  activity (green) represents the sum of all detected monomeric products. The undetected product (red)
#  represents the fraction of the consumed substrate that was not accounted for by the quantified
#  peroxygenase products. This fraction may correspond to peroxidase-derived products that were not
#  scavenged by ascorbic acid (e.g., dimers observed in reactions with MorUPO, MroUPO, AtuUPO and HspUPO)
#  or to compounds that remained undetectable by GC-MS."
#  CAVEAT: "undetected product" is NOT a clean peroxidase measurement. It pools genuine peroxidase-derived
#  product with anything GC-MS could not see. Treat the green column as the T1 signal; do not treat the
#  red column as a peroxidase rate.
#  Figure label -> full name mapping follows Table S1. PaDaI in the figure = PaDa-I.
